name: Next KPI
description: Next Collection family of ten current-generation KPI tiles chosen with Style, covering four directions. Motion: Ticker (odometer digit wheels that spin when scrolled into view), Beam (travelling border beam over a dot grid) and Liquid Fill (tile fills with a moving wave up to Percent). Depth: Tilt (pointer tilt with a floating number plate) and Flip Detail (front figure, back comparison and breakdown). Bold: Neo Brutal, Clay and Aurora Glow. Smart: Bento Tile (container queries recompose number, sparkline, change and ring into bento sub-tiles) and Adaptive (switches between chip, big-number and row layouts by its own width). Effects follow Magic UI patterns (number-ticker, border-beam, magic-card) rebuilt on Universal Theme variables, so every tile follows Vita, Vita Dark, Redwood and Theme Roller changes.
helpText: Pick a Style, then map Label and Value (formatted in SQL with the application's NLS settings). Change and Trend (up, down or flat) add a trend indicator. Percent (0 to 100) drives Liquid Fill, the Bento Tile ring and the Adaptive bar. Series (comma-separated numbers) draws the sparkline of Tilt, Aurora Glow and Bento Tile and the bars of Neo Brutal. Compare Value, Compare Label and Breakdown fill the back of Flip Detail. Every style is complete without JavaScript; the runtime file only adds the ticker, the pointer tilt, sparklines and the Percent level.

attributes.name: Style
attributes.helpText: The tile design, grouped by direction. Motion - Ticker: odometer digit wheels spin to the value when the tile scrolls into view. Motion - Beam: a light beam travels around the border. Motion - Liquid Fill: the tile fills with a moving wave up to Percent. Depth - Tilt: the tile tilts toward the pointer and the number floats on its own layer. Depth - Flip Detail: hover or focus turns the tile to show Compare Value and Breakdown. Bold - Neo Brutal: ink border, hard shadow, flat fills, bars from Series. Bold - Clay: soft pillowy surface with inner and outer shadows. Bold - Aurora Glow: dark aurora tile with a glowing number. Smart - Bento Tile: container queries recompose number, sparkline, change and ring into bento sub-tiles. Smart - Adaptive: becomes a chip, a big number or a row depending on its own width. Under reduced motion every effect stops and the static design stays.

attributes.name: Label
attributes.helpText: Name of the metric, for example Monthly Revenue. Rendered as the tile heading.

attributes.name: Value
attributes.helpText: The key figure as display text. Format it in SQL, for example to_char(amount, 'FML999G999G990'), so it follows the application's NLS settings. The Ticker style spins every digit 0 to 9 in place and keeps separators, signs and letters as they are.

attributes.name: Unit
attributes.helpText: Optional unit shown after the value, for example SAR, %, h or orders.

attributes.name: Change
attributes.helpText: Optional change text such as +12.4% or -9. Leave empty to hide the trend indicator.

attributes.name: Trend
attributes.helpText: Direction of the change: up, down or flat. Any other value renders as flat. Up is shown in the success color and down in the danger color unless Down Is Good is set; the direction is also announced as text.

attributes.name: Down Is Good
attributes.helpText: Swap the trend colors so a decrease is shown as positive, for example for costs, churn or error rates.

attributes.name: Percent
attributes.helpText: A number from 0 to 100 with a period as decimal separator, for example 72 or 64.5. Liquid Fill uses it as the liquid level, Bento Tile as a ring sub-tile and Adaptive as a progress bar. Values outside the range are clamped; non-numeric values show an empty level.

attributes.name: Series
attributes.helpText: Comma-separated numbers, oldest first, with a period as decimal separator, for example 12,18,15,22,27. Tilt, Aurora Glow and Bento Tile draw a sparkline, Neo Brutal draws chunky bars. Up to 24 values are used. Build it in SQL with listagg.

attributes.name: Compare Value
attributes.helpText: Flip Detail back face: the reference figure, for example last quarter's value or the target. Format it in SQL like Value.

attributes.name: Compare Label
attributes.helpText: Caption for Compare Value, for example Q2 2026 or Target. Defaults to Previous.

attributes.name: Breakdown
attributes.helpText: Flip Detail back face: parts of the figure separated by |, each written as name: value, for example Riyadh: 540K|Jeddah: 410K|Dammam: 334K. The runtime file turns it into a list of name and value pairs; without JavaScript the text stays readable as is.

attributes.name: Icon
attributes.helpText: Optional Font APEX icon class, for example fa-line-chart. Shown beside the label; Clay and Adaptive give it a larger badge.

attributes.name: Description
attributes.helpText: Optional footnote, for example vs. last month or rolling 30 days.

attributes.name: Row Lower Is Better
attributes.helpText: Accepts Y, yes, true or 1 (lower is better: a decrease is shown as good) and N, no, false or 0 (higher is better), in upper, lower or title case. A row value wins over the region switch for that row. Leave it empty to use the region's Down Is Good switch. Map it to a column so each row decides, for example case when kpi_code in ('COST','ERRORS') then 'Y' end.
